summary.goal:
Build a small library management system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies), with a command-line interface, persistence, validation, tests and documentation.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/library.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>` to use another file. Create the file on first use. Ids are integers assigned in order per entity type, starting at 1.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/books.js: addBook({ title, author, copies = 1 }), listBooks({ available } = {}); a book is { id, title, author, copies, available }.
- src/members.js: addMember({ name }); a member is { id, name }.
- src/loans.js: checkout({ bookId, memberId, days = 14, today }), returnLoan({ loanId, today }), listLoans({ memberId, overdue, today } = {}), report({ today }). A loan is { id, bookId, memberId, out, due, returned: null | date, fine }. Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date. Rules: checkout fails when the book has no available copy or the member already has 3 active loans; returning a loan after its due date charges a fine of 0.50 per day late, capped at 20.00; returning a loan twice fails.

CLI: bin/library.js, run as `node bin/library.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints one JSON value on stdout and exits 0. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2 (unknown command or missing option: exit 1).
- `add-book --title <t> --author <a> [--copies <n>]` prints the book.
- `add-member --name <n>` prints the member.
- `checkout --book <id> --member <id> [--days <n>] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan.
- `return --loan <id> [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan with its fine.
- `list-books [--available]` prints an array of books.
- `list-loans [--member <id>] [--overdue] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints an array of loans (`--overdue` keeps only active loans whose due date is before today).
- `report [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints { books, copies, available, members, activeLoans, overdue, finesOwed } where finesOwed is the sum of the fines of every returned loan.

Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs every test, and write a README.md that documents the modules, every command with an example, and the rules. npm test must pass.

tasks.title: Foundation: npm test script, JSON store and shared helpers
tasks.spec:
Create the shared foundation described in the design (sections 'Persistence' and 'Testing') so the other modules can be written against a frozen interface.

Deliverables:
1. package.json: add "scripts": { "test": "node --test" }. Change nothing else (keep name/version/type).
2. .gitignore: keep node_modules/ and .magic/, add data/ so runtime library files are not committed.
3. src/store.js: exactly the exports and semantics in the design's 'Persistence - src/store.js' section: DEFAULT_DATA_PATH, emptyState, loadState, saveState, updateState, nextId, todayISO, isValidDate, assertDate, addDays, daysBetween, round2, isActiveLoan, isOverdueLoan, availableCopies, bookView. Synchronous fs, create parent directories on write, missing file -> emptyState(), invalid JSON or non-object JSON -> Error('invalid data file: <path>'), normalize missing arrays/counters on load as described. Dates use UTC arithmetic internally so addDays never drifts across DST; todayISO uses local date components.
4. test/store.test.js: node:test + node:assert/strict, each test using its own directory from fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'library-')). Cover: missing file returns empty state and does not create the file; saveState creates nested parent directories and writes JSON that loadState reads back; updateState returns the mutator's value and persists; nextId returns 1, 2, 3 per kind and keeps the counters independent; normalization of a file with missing keys (and nextIds derived from max id); Error('invalid data file: <path>') for a corrupt file; todayISO(new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 5, 12))) style checks; addDays across a month end and a year boundary; isValidDate rejects 2026-2-3, 2026-02-30, 2026-13-01, '', null; daysBetween both directions; isActiveLoan/isOverdueLoan; availableCopies and bookView with one active and one returned loan.

Boundaries: do not create the domain modules, the CLI or the README. Never write to data/library.json from a test.

acceptance.review: Confirm `npm test` actually executes test/store.test.js (Node prints the test/assertion counts; zero discovered files is a failure even though the exit code is 0) and that all listed exports exist with the documented semantics. Confirm no test touches the repository's data/library.json.

decisions: Store path is resolved as `data ?? DEFAULT_DATA_PATH` before calling updateState/loadState: loadState has a default parameter but saveState does not, so relying on module defaults would break the no-`data` case. DEFAULT_DATA_PATH is imported from src/store.js, which keeps the module's only dependency the store.
Validation rejects non-string as well as blank title/author with the same 'title is required' / 'author is required' messages, so a non-string input cannot reach .trim() and leak a TypeError.
copies is checked with Number.isInteger(copies) && copies >= 1, so 1.5, '2', 0, negative and NaN values all produce 'copies must be a positive integer'; an omitted copies still defaults to 1.

The value returned by addBook is a fresh object spread from the stored record, so the object held in state.books never gains an `available` key and the persisted file stays clean (asserted in the test by scanning the raw file text).
listBooks sorts defensively by id even though books are appended in id order, so the documented ordering holds regardless of how the file was produced.

tasks.title: CLI: parse arguments, dispatch commands, map errors to exit codes
tasks.spec:
Build the command line exactly as described in the design's 'CLI contract' section.

src/cli.js: export `class UsageError extends Error` (used only for exit-1 cases) and `run(argv)` which parses argv and calls the domain modules, returning the value to print (a book, a member, a loan, or an array/report object) and throwing on any failure. Parse: first non-flag token is the command; `--data <path>` is accepted anywhere and defaults to data/library.json; flags with values are --title, --author, --copies, --name, --book, --member, --loan, --days, --today; --available and --overdue are booleans; repeated flags keep the last value; unknown option -> Error('unknown option: <flag>'); missing value (no following token, or the next token starts with '--') -> UsageError('missing value for <flag>'); missing required option -> UsageError('missing option: <flag>'); no command -> UsageError('missing command'); unknown command -> UsageError('unknown command: <cmd>'). Integer options (--book, --member, --loan, --copies, --days) are parsed strictly and throw Error('invalid value for <flag>: <value>') when not an integer. Map --data to the `data` option of every domain call and --today to `today`.

bin/library.js: `#!/usr/bin/env node`; call run(process.argv.slice(2)); on success write JSON.stringify(value) + '\n' to stdout and exit 0; on a thrown error write JSON.stringify({ error: err.message }) + '\n' to stderr and exit 1 for UsageError, 2 otherwise. Nothing else goes to stdout.

test/cli.test.js (node:test, node:assert/strict, child_process.spawnSync with process.execPath and a temp --data path per test): cover every command and both flags; assert the printed JSON values, the exit codes 0/1/2 and that failures print { error } on stderr with empty stdout; one test runs a full workflow (add-book, add-member, checkout with --days and --today, list-books --available, list-loans --overdue --today, return --today with a fine, report --today) against a single data file and checks the report numbers; one test checks that ids and data survive across separate invocations.

acceptance.review: Run a few commands by hand and confirm: exit 0 with one JSON value on stdout on success; exit 1 only for unknown command and missing option/value; exit 2 for domain errors, unknown options and invalid values; the data file is created on first use and `--data` redirects everything.

report.summary: Built the command-line layer per the design's "CLI contract". `src/cli.js` exports `UsageError extends Error` and `run(argv)`: it scans argv for the first non-flag token as the command, accepts `--data <path>` anywhere (defaulting to `data/library.json` from the store module), treats `--available`/`--overdue` as booleans, keeps the last value of repeated flags, and rejects unknown options (`Error('unknown option: <flag>')`, exit 2) and missing/invalid values (`UsageError('missing value for <flag>')` and missing required options `UsageError('missing option: <flag>')`, exit 1). Integer options (`--book`, `--member`, `--loan`, `--copies`, `--days`) are parsed with a strict `/^-?\d+$/` check throwing `Error('invalid value for <flag>: <value>')` (exit 2), while `--today` is only required to be present and its format is validated by the loans module. Each command builds the exact options object its domain function documents and returns its value. `bin/library.js` is a thin `#!/usr/bin/env node` driver that calls `run(process.argv.slice(2))`, writes `JSON.stringify(value)+'\n'` to stdout (exit 0) or `JSON.stringify({error: err.message})+'\n'` to stderr (exit 1 for UsageError, 2 otherwise), using `process.exitCode` so the write is never truncated; nothing else reaches stdout. `test/cli.test.js` has 23 node:test cases spawning `process.execPath` on the binary with a per-test temp `--data` path, covering every command, both boolean flags, exit codes 0/1/2, empty stdout on failure, a full workflow against one data file, id/data persistence across invocations, and that the store file is created only on first write.
report.evidence: `node --test test/cli.test.js` -> 23 tests, 23 pass, 0 fail. `npm test` (the acceptance command) -> 81 tests, 81 pass, 0 fail, exit 0; no `data/` directory is created in the repo by the tests. Manual runs confirmed: success prints one compact JSON value with exit 0; `frobnicate` -> exit 1 `{"error":"unknown command: frobnicate"}`; missing `--author` -> exit 1 `missing option: --author`; `--bogus` -> exit 2 `unknown option: --bogus`; `--book abc` -> exit 2 `invalid value for --book: abc`; `--today garbage` -> exit 2 `invalid date: garbage`; `--title` at end of argv -> exit 1 `missing value for --title`; from a fresh temp cwd a bare `add-book` created `data/library.json` and the next invocation read it back; `--data <path>` (including before the command) redirected the store to a separate temp file.
decisions: Extra positional tokens (non-command, not starting with '--') are ignored rather than erroring, since the spec only defines 'unknown option' for '--'-prefixed tokens and no command takes positional arguments.

A known value flag used with a command that does not need it (e.g. `report --title x`) is accepted and ignored; only flags outside the global list produce 'unknown option', matching the design's definition of that error.

Negative integers parse successfully via the strict integer check and then fail inside the domain module (e.g. `--copies -1` -> exit 2 'copies must be a positive integer'), keeping value-syntax errors and domain errors distinct.
bin/library.js sets process.exitCode instead of calling process.exit() immediately, so the stdout/stderr write completes before the process ends.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented src/loans.js (checkout, returnLoan, listLoans, report) against the frozen src/store.js only, plus test/loans.test.js with 18 node:test cases. No imports of books.js/members.js: books, members and loans are read and written through state fields loaded via store.updateState/loadState.

Behavior: checkout resolves `out = today ?? todayISO()`, asserts the date, then requires a positive-integer `days` (default 14), and inside updateState checks in the documented order — book exists, member exists, a free copy (availableCopies > 0), fewer than 3 active loans for that member — before pushing { id, bookId, memberId, out, due: addDays(out, days), returned: null, fine: 0 } with the id from nextId(state, 'loan') and returning a copy of the stored record. returnLoan rejects unknown and already-returned loans, then sets returned = today and fine = late > 0 ? min(20, round2(late * 0.5)) : 0 with late = daysBetween(loan.due, today). listLoans copies the loans, filters by memberId and, when truthy, by isOverdueLoan(loan, today), and sorts ascending by id. report counts books, sums copies and derived availability, counts members, active and overdue loans, and sums the fines of returned loans only through round2.

Testing: fixtures are seeded straight into the store with updateState (no other module imported), each test uses its own fs.mkdtempSync directory and passes an explicit `today`; the repository's data/library.json is never touched (verified: no data/ directory exists after the run).

Built the command-line layer per the design's "CLI contract". `src/cli.js` exports `UsageError extends Error` and `run(argv)`: it scans argv for the first non-flag token as the command, accepts `--data <path>` anywhere (defaulting to `data/library.json` from the store module), treats `--available`/`--overdue` as booleans, keeps the last value of repeated flags, and rejects unknown options (`Error('unknown option: <flag>')`, exit 2) and missing/invalid values (`UsageError('missing value for <flag>')` and missing required options `UsageError('missing option: <flag>')`, exit 1). Integer options (`--book`, `--member`, `--loan`, `--copies`, `--days`) are parsed with a strict `/^-?\d+$/` check throwing `Error('invalid value for <flag>: <value>')` (exit 2), while `--today` is only required to be present and its format is validated by the loans module. Each command builds the exact options object its domain function documents and returns its value. `bin/library.js` is a thin `#!/usr/bin/env node` driver that calls `run(process.argv.slice(2))`, writes `JSON.stringify(value)+'\n'` to stdout (exit 0) or `JSON.stringify({error: err.message})+'\n'` to stderr (exit 1 for UsageError, 2 otherwise), using `process.exitCode` so the write is never truncated; nothing else reaches stdout. `test/cli.test.js` has 23 node:test cases spawning `process.execPath` on the binary with a per-test temp `--data` path, covering every command, both boolean flags, exit codes 0/1/2, empty stdout on failure, a full workflow against one data file, id/data persistence across invocations, and that the store file is created only on first write.

Wrote README.md documenting the finished library system. It covers: (1) what the project is, Node >= 18 / ES modules / zero dependencies, and `npm test`; (2) the storage model — one JSON file, default `data/library.json` relative to the current directory, created on first use, `--data <path>` accepted by every command (anywhere on the line, last value wins), sequential per-entity ids, plus the pretty-printed file shape and the note that `available` is derived and never stored; (3) all four modules (src/store.js, src/books.js, src/members.js, src/loans.js) with exported signatures, returned shapes and the `data` option; (4) all seven CLI commands with exact usage lines, a copy-pasteable example with real output for each, and a full 10-command end-to-end session in a temp data file; (5) the rules — 14-day default, checkout failure without an available copy or at 3 concurrent loans, 0.50/day late fine capped at 20.00 charged at return (with a worked cap example), no double returns, and the exact overdue definition (active and due strictly before today); (6) the error table (exit 0 success, 1 unknown command / missing option or value, 2 everything else) with real error examples. No source or test files were modified; README.md is the only file I created.
